prompt: I would like to outperform the S&P 500 in the next year. Can you propose 10 stocks I should buy?
reply:
# 10 Stock Ideas for the Next Year

No one can reliably pick stocks that beat the S&P 500. In a typical year most professional large-cap fund managers underperform it, and over 10–15 years about 90% do. A 10-stock portfolio will perform very differently from the index, which could mean beating it or trailing it by a wide margin.

My information only runs to May 2026, so I don't know current prices, valuations or news. Treat these as **ideas to research**, not a buy list.

## The list

| # | Company | Why it could outperform | Main risk |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM)** | Makes nearly all leading-edge AI chips (Nvidia, Apple, AMD, Broadcom) and has strong pricing power | Taiwan–China tensions; chip cycles |
| 2 | **Broadcom (AVGO)** | Custom AI chips for hyperscalers, AI networking, and cash flow from VMware software | High valuation; depends on a few large customers |
| 3 | **Alphabet (GOOGL)** | Search profits fund Gemini, Google Cloud and its own AI chips; Waymo is upside | Antitrust remedies; AI eroding search |
| 4 | **Amazon (AMZN)** | AWS growth from AI demand, rising retail margins, fast-growing ad business | Heavy spending on data centers reduces free cash flow |
| 5 | **Eli Lilly (LLY)** | Leader in obesity and diabetes drugs (GLP-1s), with an oral version in its pipeline | Expensive stock; US drug-pricing pressure; competition |
| 6 | **GE Vernova (GEV)** | Gas turbines and grid equipment in high demand as data centers drive electricity use | Stock has already risen a lot; wind business problems |
| 7 | **Vertiv (VRT)** | Power and liquid-cooling equipment for data centers | Swings sharply with AI spending; volatile |
| 8 | **JPMorgan Chase (JPM)** | Best-in-class bank with strong buybacks; benefits from lighter regulation and deal activity | Recession or rising loan losses |
| 9 | **Uber (UBER)** | Now solidly profitable, buying back shares, and partnering with robotaxi companies | Robotaxis could bypass its platform |
| 10 | **Mastercard (MA)** | Earns a fee on global card spending; steady, reliable growth | Regulation of card fees; new payment methods |

**Concentration warning:** six of these (TSM, AVGO, GOOGL, AMZN, GEV, VRT) depend on the same trend: AI and data-center spending. If that spending slows, they could fall together. LLY, JPM, UBER and MA add some variety, but this portfolio is still aggressive.

## How to use it more safely

- **Core–satellite approach:** put most of your money (e.g., 70–80%) in an S&P 500 index fund and use the rest for picks like these. You still have a chance to beat the index without risking badly trailing it.
- **Equal-weight the picks** (about 10% each) and rebalance once or twice a year so no single stock dominates.
- **Check valuations before buying.** Some of these may have risen or fallen sharply since my information ends, which changes the case for them.
- **Write down your reason for each stock** and decide in advance what would make you sell.
- **Consider taxes.** In many countries, gains on holdings kept less than a year are taxed more heavily.
- **One year is short.** Luck plays a big role over 12 months, so judge the strategy over several years.

If you tell me your country, how much you plan to invest, your risk tolerance and what you already own, I can adjust the list. For example, I could make it less AI-heavy, add dividend payers, or suggest ETFs available where you live. For decisions involving significant money, a licensed financial adviser is worth consulting.
